text:
Predicates:
MultipleBirth(x) ::: x is born in a multiple birth.
Siblings(x) ::: x has siblings who were born together.
AnnoyingSiblings(x) ::: x complains often about annoying siblings.
Strangers(x) ::: x lives with strangers.
Home(x) ::: x lives at home.
Baby(x) ::: x is a baby.
Premises:
∀x (MultipleBirth(x) → Siblings(x)) ::: People who are born in a multiple birth with siblings spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings.
∀x (Siblings(x) → MultipleBirth(x)) ::: If people have siblings who were born together, then they were born in a multiple birth.
∀x (AnnoyingSiblings(x) → Siblings(x)) ::: If people complain often about annoying siblings, then they have siblings who were born together.
∀x (Home(x) → ¬Strangers(x)) ::: If people live at home, then they do not live with strangers.
∀x (Siblings(x) → Home(x)) ::: If people spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings, then they often live at home.
(Baby(luke) ∧ MultipleBirth(luke) ∧ Strangers(luke)) ⊕ (¬Baby(luke) ∧ ¬MultipleBirth(luke) ∧ ¬Strangers(luke)) ::: Luke either is a baby born in a multiple birth and lives with strangers, or is not a baby born in a multiple birth and does not live with strangers.
Conclusion:
¬MultipleBirth(luke) ∧ ¬AnnoyingSiblings(luke) ::: Luke is neither born in a multiple birth nor complains often about annoying siblings.
